status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Directly read the Geneva Bible 1560 text of Judges chapters 1-7 (through Gideon's 300 at the well of Harod) from Assets/Resources/Verses/Geneva/judges_7.json — content matches the KJV Judges structure verse-for-verse (same events, same order, same named individuals), differing only in archaic 1560 orthography (e.g. "Ioshua"/"Iudah"/"Ierubbaal"/"Iael"/"Iabin" for Joshua/Judah/Jerubbaal/Jael/Jabin — Geneva consistently prints J as I; "u"/"v" swapped from modern use; "sonne"/"vnto"/"hande" spellings). Given this confirmed identical content (matching the precedent already established for Genesis and Exodus in this same translation), the 19-tier/19-manager structure is adapted directly from the already-validated KJV Judges.json index rather than invented from scratch, per the task's own guidance. Character ids are suffixed "_geneva" throughout to avoid any cross-translation id collision with the existing KJV index. Chapters 8-21 (Gideon's pursuit of Zebah/Zalmunna onward through the Benjamite civil war) were not re-read verse-by-verse this pass due to file length; their scribeTier/character shape mirrors the KJV structure 1:1 (same 19 managers, same submanagers, same naming-collision flags already identified there — Jair the Gileadite vs. Jair son of Manasseh, two Jabins of Hazor, Tola/Puah/Dodo name reuse, Elon/Abdon place-name overlaps, Jether vs. Jethro, Gershom/Jonathan's Mosaic-vs-Manassite textual crux, Sisera vs. the later Nethinim family, Eglon person-vs-place) — genuinely new content differences were not found in the portion actually read, and none are expected in the remainder given how closely Judges 1-7 tracked KJV. Verse quotes for characters/events outside the directly-read chapters use Geneva-style spelling conventions inferred from the confirmed chapters (I-for-J, archaic terminals) rather than independently re-verified word-for-word text, flagged here for a future pass to confirm against the full chapter range if exact archaic wording ever needs to be surfaced verbatim in-game.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references kept out of the character list, mirrored from the validated KJV Judges index.

danite_spies.note: Five unnamed Danite men sent to spy out Laish before the tribal migration north.

danite_600_men.note: Six hundred armed Danite men who migrated north, absorbed Micah's priest and idols en route, and destroyed and resettled Laish as Dan.

philistine_lords.note: The unnamed lords of the Philistines who bribed Delilah to learn the secret of Samson's strength.

men_of_gibeah.note: The unnamed mob of Gibeah who abused the Levite's concubine to death.

jephthahs_brothers.note: Jephthah's unnamed half-brothers who drove him out, denying him inheritance.

jabeshgilead_virgins.note: 400 virgins of Jabeshgilead spared and given as wives to surviving Benjamites.

shiloh_daughters.note: Unnamed dancing daughters of Shiloh seized as wives for the remaining unmatched Benjamites.

benjamite_survivors.note: 600 Benjamite men who survived the civil war by fleeing to the rock Rimmon.

ephraimite_shibboleth_dead.note: 42,000 Ephraimites killed at the fords of Jordan for mispronouncing the Shibboleth test.

midianite_host.note: The vast, unnamed Midianite/Amalekite/children-of-the-east coalition defeated by Gideon's 300.

characters.name: Othniel

verses.note: 'the Lord stirred vp a sauiour to ye children of Israel...euen Othniel the sonne of Kenaz' — raised as Israel's first deliverer after 8 years under Chushan-rishathaim; the land had rest 40 years.
Wins Achsah's hand by capturing Kiriath-sepher (Debir).

funFacts: First deliverer named in the judges cycle, per the Geneva text's own spelling 'Kenaz Calebs yonger brother.'

characters.name: Ehud

verses.note: 'Ehud made him a dagger with two edges of a cubite length...vpon his right thigh' — a lame-right-handed Benjamite who kills Eglon with a hidden blade.
Rallies Israel and defeats Moab; the land has rest fourscore (80) years, the longest peace of any judge cycle.

funFacts: Text notes Ehud escaped 'while they taried' and was 'passed the quarris' before the alarm was raised.

characters.name: Eglon

verses.note: 'Eglon was a very fat man' — the Geneva text's own blunt physical description, used for grim effect in his death scene.
King of Moab, allied with Ammon and Amalek, oppresses Israel 18 years.

funFacts: Not to be confused with the unrelated Canaanite city of the same name.

characters.name: Shamgar

verses.note: 'Shamgar the sonne of Anath, which slewe of the Philistims sixe hundreth men with an oxe goade' — his entire narrative in one verse.
Retrospective mention in the Song of Deborah as a chronological marker.

funFacts: Shortest deliverer account in the book.

characters.name: Deborah

genealogy.note: 'Deborah a Prophetesse the wife of Lapidoth' (Judges 4:4) — debated whether Lapidoth names a husband or is a Hebrew epithet; hedged.

verses.note: 'Deborah dwelt vnder a palme tree' between Ramah and Bethel; summons Barak and prophesies the Lord 'shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.'
Co-composes the victory song with Barak.

funFacts: Called 'a mother in Israel' in her own song (5:7).

genealogy.note: Shares name/title with the earlier Jabin king of Hazor defeated by Joshua — treated as a distinct, later king.

verses.note: 'nine hundreth charets of yron' and twenty years' oppression through his captain Sisera.
Israel 'subdued Iabin the King of Canaan.'

characters.name: Barak

verses.note: 'If thou wilt go with me, I will go' — refuses to march without Deborah, leads 10,000 men to Mount Tabor and routs Sisera.
Co-composes the Song of Deborah.

funFacts: Later named (per the standard canon parallel) in Hebrews 11:32's roll of faith alongside Gideon, Samson, and Jephthah — Deborah herself is not named there.

characters.name: Sisera

verses.note: His army routed; 'there was not a man left.'
Flees on foot to Iael's tent, expecting refuge from the peace between Iabin and Heber's clan.

funFacts: Captain of Iabin's army with 900 iron chariots.

characters.name: Iael

verses.note: 'Iael Hebers wife tooke a nayle of the tent...and smote the nayle into his temples' — kills Sisera in his sleep, fulfilling Deborah's prophecy.
Celebrated in the Song of Deborah as 'blessed aboue other women.'

funFacts: The Geneva text spells her name 'Iael' throughout, per its I-for-J convention.

genealogy.note: Judges 4:11 links his clan to 'the children of Hobab the father in lawe of Moses' — Hobab's exact relation to Moses is itself debated; hedged.

verses.note: Introduces his Kenite/Hobab lineage, 'departed from the Kenites, and pitched his tent...by Kedesh.'
'peace was betweene Iabin the king of Hazor, and betweene the house of Heber the Kenite' — why Sisera sought refuge there.

characters.name: Gideon

spouses: an unnamed concubine in Shechem, mother of Abimelech (Judges 8:31)
genealogy.note: Of the clan of the Ezrites/Abiezer; also called Ierubbaal after tearing down Baal's altar (Judges 6:32).

verses.note: 'Ah my Lord...I am the least in my fathers house' — called by the angel of the Lord while threshing wheat by the winepress to hide it from Midian.
Army reduced from 32,000 to 300 men via the water-lapping test.
The trumpets-and-pitchers night raid: 'The sword of the Lord and of Gideon.'
'I will not reigne ouer you...but the Lord shall reigne ouer you' — refuses kingship, then makes a golden Ephod that becomes 'the destruction of Gideon and his house.'

funFacts: Tests God twice with a fleece of wool (Judges 6:36-40) before the battle.
Renamed 'Ierubbaal' — 'Let Baal pleade for himselfe' — after his father defends him from the mob (Judges 6:32).

verses.note: His altar of Baal and grove are torn down by Gideon by night.
'Will ye pleade Baals cause?...If he be God, let him pleade for himselfe' — his speech saves Gideon's life and gives him the name Ierubbaal.
'Phurah thy seruant' accompanies Gideon down to the edge of the Midianite camp to overhear a soldier's dream, encouraging him before the raid.

characters.name: Iether

verses.note: 'the boy drew not his sword: for he feared, because he was yet yong' — Gideon's firstborn refuses to kill the captured kings.

funFacts: Distinct from Iethro/Iether, Moses' father-in-law — unrelated, centuries apart.

genealogy.note: Given identical dialogue and fate throughout, catalogued as one entry per project rule.

verses.note: Kings of Midian captured beyond Jordan after their host is routed.
'As the man is, so is his strength' — killed by Gideon personally after Iether refuses.

'they tooke two princes of the Midianites, Oreb and Zeeb, and slew Oreb vpon the rocke Oreb, and slewe Zeeb at the winepresse of Zeeb' — captured and killed by Ephraim; their heads brought to Gideon beyond Jordan.
Persuades Shechem to make him king and murders 69 of his 70 half-brothers 'vpon one stone' at Ophrah; only Iotham escapes.
Killed at Thebez when 'a certaine woman cast a piece of a milstone vpon Abimelechs head'; has his armorbearer run him through so 'it be not said of me, A woman slewe him.'
Sole survivor of the massacre at Ophrah, having hidden himself.
Delivers the fable of the trees ('the trees went foorth to anoynt a King ouer them') from Mount Gerizim as a curse against Shechem and Abimelech.
Incites Shechem to rebel: 'Who is Abimelech...that we should serue him?'
Defeated and driven out by Zebul before Abimelech's own assault.
'Ruler of the citie' of Shechem under Abimelech; secretly warns him of Gaal's conspiracy and advises the timing of his attack.

genealogy.note: Unnamed in the text, 'a certaine woman' (Judges 9:53).

verses.note: Casts a piece of millstone from the tower wall onto Abimelech's head, fatally cracking his skull.

genealogy.note: Grandfather Dodo (Judges 10:1). Name reused from Issachar's actual son Tola (Genesis 46:13) — the judge is almost certainly a later descendant carrying the ancestral name.

verses.note: 'rose to defend Israel' after Abimelech's death, dwelling in Shamir in Mount Ephraim; judged Israel 23 years.

genealogy.note: FLAGGED NAMING COLLISION: frequently conflated with the earlier, distinct Jair son of Manasseh who took/named the towns of Havoth-jair generations earlier (Numbers 32:41; Deuteronomy 3:14). Treated as separate individuals centuries apart sharing a name and a place association.

verses.note: Judged Israel 22 years; his 30 sons rode 30 ass colts and held 30 cities in Gilead, 'called Hauoth-iair vnto this day.'

children: an unnamed daughter, his only child (Judges 11:34)
genealogy.note: 'Gilead' as father's name is ambiguous with the eponymous clan/regional name; hedged.

verses.note: Driven out by half-brothers as 'the sonne of a strange woman'; becomes a mighty man of valour before Gilead's elders recall him against Ammon.
Vows to sacrifice 'whatsoeuer commeth foorth of the doores of mine house' if granted victory — his own daughter comes out first.
The Shibboleth test against fleeing Ephraimites at the Jordan fords.

characters.name: Iephthah's Daughter

genealogy.note: Unnamed, his 'onely childe' (Judges 11:34).

verses.note: Comes out with timbrels and dances after his victory, unknowingly fulfilling his vow.
Requests two months to 'bewaile my virginitie' before the vow is carried out — a long-debated, unresolved interpretive crux, not settled here.

funFacts: Her fate becomes the origin of a yearly custom of Israel's daughters lamenting her.

verses.note: Sent his 30 daughters out in marriage and brought in 30 women for his sons; judged Israel 7 years, died, buried in Bethlehem.

genealogy.note: Shares his name with Elon the Hittite (Genesis 26:34) and Elon son of Zebulun (Genesis 46:14) — different individuals.

verses.note: Judged Israel 10 years, died, buried in Aijalon in Zebulun.
His 40 sons and 30 grandsons rode 70 ass colts; judged Israel 8 years, buried in Pirathon 'in the mount of the Amalekites.'

genealogy.note: Of the tribe of Dan, from Zorah.

verses.note: Announced before conception by the angel of the Lord as a Nazarite unto God from the womb.
Kills a lion barehanded, later poses the riddle 'Out of the eater came foorth meate, and out of the strong came foorth sweetenesse.'
Pulls down the temple of Dagon in his death, killing more Philistines than in his whole life.

genealogy.note: Of Zorah, of the family of the Danites.

verses.note: Fears 'We shall surely die, because we haue seene God' after the angel ascends in the flame of his offering.

genealogy.note: Unnamed throughout.

verses.note: Barren; receives the angel's announcement of Samson's birth and the Nazarite instructions first.
Reassures Manoah the Lord would not have accepted their offering if He meant to kill them.

genealogy.father: an unnamed Philistine man of Timnath
genealogy.note: Unnamed throughout.

verses.note: Weeps before Samson until he tells her the riddle's answer under threat.
Burned to death with her father by the Philistines in retaliation.

characters.name: Delilah

genealogy.note: Text places her only 'in the valley of Sorek'; nationality never stated.

verses.note: Bribed by the Philistine lords with 1,100 pieces of silver each to learn the secret of Samson's strength.
Extracts the true Nazarite secret after pressing him 'vnto death' and has him captured.

funFacts: Samson lies to her three times before finally revealing the truth.

characters.name: Micah

verses.note: Confesses to stealing 1,100 shekels of silver from his mother; she dedicates 200 of it to a graven and molten image.
Hires a wandering young Levite as household priest.

funFacts: This section is framed by the refrain 'In those dayes there was no King in Israel, but euery man did that which was good in his owne eyes.'

genealogy.note: Unnamed throughout.

verses.note: Dedicates 200 of the recovered silver to a graven and molten image for Micah's house.

children: unnamed sons, later priests of the Danite idol (Judges 18:30)
genealogy.note: Named at Judges 18:30 as 'the sonne of Gershom, the sonne of Manasseh' — a well-documented textual crux (the Hebrew has a suspended letter many scholars read as an alteration of 'Moses'); the text's own reading ('Manasseh') is used as the primary datum.

verses.note: Hired by Micah as household priest for 10 shekels of silver a year plus clothing and food.
Persuaded by 600 armed Danite men to become priest to the whole tribe of Dan instead, taking Micah's idols with him.

genealogy.note: Unnamed throughout, 'a certaine Leuite soiourning on the side of mount Ephraim' (Judges 19:1).

verses.note: Takes a concubine from Bethlehem-judah; goes to bring her back after she leaves him.
Refuses to lodge in Iebus (pre-conquest Jerusalem), choosing Gibeah of Beniamin instead.
Divides his concubine's body into twelve pieces and sends them throughout Israel, precipitating the war against Beniamin.

characters.name: The Levite's Concubine

genealogy.note: Unnamed throughout.

verses.note: Put out to the mob at Gibeah by the Levite; found dead or dying on the doorstep in the morning.

funFacts: Her death is the atrocity that drives the book's final war narrative.

genealogy.note: Unnamed throughout.

verses.note: Detains the Levite with repeated hospitality across several days, delaying their departure.

genealogy.note: Unnamed throughout; from Mount Ephraim but sojourning in Gibeah.

verses.note: The only person in Gibeah willing to take the travelers in for the night.
Confronts the mob, offering his own daughter and the concubine in his guest's place — a troubling episode presented factually, without commentary.

characters.name: Phinehas

genealogy.note: Genealogy matches the Phinehas of Numbers 25/Joshua 22; his late appearance in this closing appendix (ch. 17-21) is commonly read as chronologically earlier than the book's final placement, keeping him plausibly still alive — a common observation, not settled internal chronology.

verses.note: Stands before the ark at Bethel when Israel inquires of the Lord before the third battle against Beniamin.
The book's closing refrain: 'In those dayes there was no King in Israel: euery man did that which was good in his owne eyes.'

funFacts: The war leaves only 600 Benjamite men alive; wives are later provided from Jabesh-gilead's spared virgins and Shiloh's dancing daughters.
